and the rest is my offering of purity. The ewe lamb as sin offering and the ram as peace offering come to complete the obligation of the nazirite's shaving of purity.

and the second and third are freewill offerings. For he has not yet become pure of his impurity (and the commentators discuss the relationship between this case and the case described above, "if I was confirmed", for it would seem possible to say that it is the same case; see Lechem Mishneh and Mirkevet HaMishneh).
the guilt offering and the burnt offering. With which both the leper and the nazirite who became impure are obligated.

do not hold back, neither in the shaving of impurity nor in leprosy. Unlike the sin offering, these offerings do not hold back the nazirite from beginning to count a pure nazirite period (as above 6:12) and the leper from eating sacred offerings (see also Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 1:5).
he was purified with the birds. In his first shaving, in the manner of the purification of a leper.
and the bird sin offering is his sin offering. The sin offering he brings at his second shaving is for his leprosy.

and the animal burnt offering that is with it is from the offering of the shaving of purity. Apparently this speaks of a burnt offering he brings together with the sin offering at his second shaving, as detailed above in the condition: "and if I am pure of corpse impurity and a leper...". The commentators already found this difficult, as explained there.
the bird sin offering. That he brings at his first shaving.
and the animal burnt offering is a freewill offering. Because only now has he brought the obligation of the shaving of impurity and he must count another year of nazirite status.
and he has brought the offering of purity at the last. The commentators found it difficult why the offering of purity is brought at the last shaving and not at the second (Kesef Mishneh, Radbaz).
and the bird sin offering comes for a doubt. A doubt of corpse impurity.
when he was a minor. For example, if he was twelve years and one day old, when he reached the age of vows, and if he accepted nazirite status upon himself he is obligated in it (above 2:13).

he rounds the corners of his head not in a place of a mitzvah. For adult males, unlike minors and women, are commanded concerning the prohibition of rounding the corners of the head (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 12:1-3), and it was permitted to them only in a certain shaving of a mitzvah and not in a doubtful shaving (see also above 9:15).
for these four shavings are not essential but only a mitzvah. Neither for a nazirite (as above 8:2) nor for a leper (Hilchot Tum'at Tzara'at 11:4).
after he is purified from his leprosy. After the leprous affliction has healed.

he is sprinkled on the third and seventh. At the beginning of these days he shaves the first shaving of a leper, and he must be purified already within the seven days of his counting, because one impure through a corpse cannot send his offerings to the Temple (Hilchot Bi'at Mikdash 2:12), and after the sprinkling he becomes pure of corpse impurity even though he is a leper (Hilchot Parah 11:3), and on the seventh he shaves the second shaving of a leper and brings the offerings of a leper (Lechem Mishneh).

and he shaves the shaving of impurity. The commentators found it difficult why Rambam did not mention that after these seven days of his leprosy he must count a complete nazirite period, in case he is a pure nazirite, and only at its end shave the shaving of impurity, and they explained that he did mean this but abbreviated his wording (Lechem Mishneh and others).
and he became pure of the doubt of his leprosy. He healed from his doubtful leprosy.

he counts his nazirite days completely and afterwards shaves the shaving of the affliction, for the shaving of a doubtful affliction does not override nazirite status. He cannot first count seven days of impurity and shave the shaving of impurity, in case he is a leper and a leper does not send his offerings before he becomes pure of his leprosy (Hilchot Bi'at Mikdash 2:11). And on the other hand he cannot shave for his doubtful leprosy until he counts a complete nazirite period as he vowed (though it is not a definitive nazirite period, since he is impure), because a nazirite who became impure may shave only the shaving of impurity (Mirkevet HaMishneh).

if he was sprinkled on the third and seventh. During the seven days he counted for his leprosy between the first and second shaving, for without this sprinkling that purifies him from corpse impurity, he cannot send his offerings to the Temple (Hilchot Bi'at Mikdash 2:12).
and afterwards he counts another seven for corpse impurity. The reason is explained below, halakhah 13.
and is sprinkled on the third and seventh. To become pure of corpse impurity so that he can send his offerings to the Temple.
and counts seven. The seven days that a nazirite who became impure counts.
and why does he count seven. Seven additional to the seven days he counted for leprosy impurity.

for the seven days of impurity do not count within the seven days of counting between one shaving and the other of a leper. For although he became pure of corpse impurity, the obligation to count seven days because he became impure applies, and he cannot count them while he is a leper (see Lechem Mishneh).
and a nazirite vow is also among the vows of the wicked. Who do not vow nazirite status with settled mind and for the sake of Heaven (see Hilchot Nedarim 1:26).

but one who vows to the Lord in the way of holiness. Who becomes a nazirite in order to correct his deeds, for example one who is proud of his beauty and becomes a nazirite to subdue his inclination (see ibid. 13:23-25).
